model_claims.text: parse_url() refuses schemes containing a dot.
The URL is silently read as schemeless, with a.b as the host, causing requests to go to the wrong place.
model_claims.source_quote: The URL is silently read as _schemeless_, with `a.b` as the host, so a request goes to the wrong place.

model_claims.text: When the candidate scheme contains a dot and a port attempt follows the colon, parse_url keeps the schemeless reading (behavior unchanged).
model_claims.source_quote: - adds `_is_scheme_url()`, which keeps the schemeless reading when the candidate scheme contains a dot **and** a port attempt follows the colon.

model_claims.text: If a candidate scheme contains a dot and is followed by a port attempt, the schemeless interpretation is preserved.
model_claims.source_quote: - requires at least one character after the dot in the host side of that alternative, so a single label with a trailing dot (`a.:8080`) is not read as host `a.` with port 8080.

model_claims.text: Input `a.:8080` now parses as scheme `a.` with path `/8080` instead of host `a.` with port 8080.
model_claims.source_quote: - requires at least one character after the dot in the host side of that alternative, so a single label with a trailing dot (`a.:8080`) is not read as host `a.` with port 8080.

model_claims.text: Input `evil.com://good.com` is now parsed as a scheme URL with scheme `evil.com` and host `good.com` rather than as a schemeless host.
model_claims.source_quote: The `evil.com://good.com` row is the intended consequence of the feature: under RFC 3986 that string _is_ a scheme URL.

model_claims.text: Multi‑label trailing‑dot hosts such as `example.com.:8080` continue to be parsed as host and port (behavior unchanged).
model_claims.source_quote: multi-label trailing-dot hosts (`example.com.:8080`, `a.b.:443/x`) still parse as host and port.

model_rejected_claims.text: Non‑dotted candidates such as `http:80` and `mailto:12345` retain their original behavior (scheme + path).
model_rejected_claims.source_quote: - Only dotted candidates are disambiguated: `http:80` and `mailto:12345` behave exactly as before.

model_rejected_claims.text: Inputs like `example.com:8080;foo`, `example.com:8080x`, `a.b:80:90`, `example.com:8080:9090` still raise LocationParseError (behavior unchanged).
model_rejected_claims.source_quote: `example.com:8080;foo`, `example.com:8080x`, `a.b:80:90`, `example.com:8080:9090` stay in the host/port parser, so the existing validation keeps raising `LocationParseError` instead of a typo being re-read as a scheme and failing somewhere else later.
